title: ～ように／～ような — like ～, as ～
summary: Compares one thing to another: “like ～ / as ～.” ような modifies a noun (花のような人), and ように modifies a verb or adjective (花のようにきれいだ). It attaches to a noun + の or to a plain-form verb.

patterns.form: 名詞 ＋ の ＋ ような ＋ 名詞
patterns.gloss: like ～ (before a noun): 春のような暖かい日

patterns.form: 名詞 ＋ の ＋ ように ＋ 動詞／形容詞
patterns.gloss: as ～ (before a verb or adjective): 母の料理のようにおいしい

body.p: Place the thing you compare to before の and add ような or ように. ような works like an adjective that attaches to a noun, and ように works like an adverb. The standard is often something familiar, such as flowers or spring.
ような can also introduce an example: 私のような初心者 (a beginner like me), 東京のような大きな町 (a big city such as Tokyo). In this use the example is typical of the group.

examples.ja: 彼女（かのじょ）は花（はな）のような人（ひと）です。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa hana no yō na hito desu.
examples.tr: She is a person like a flower.

examples.ja: 今日（きょう）は春（はる）のような暖（あたた）かい日（ひ）です。
examples.romaji: Kyō wa haru no yō na atatakai hi desu.
examples.tr: Today is a warm day like spring.

examples.ja: 母（はは）が作（つく）る料理（りょうり）のようにおいしく作（つく）りたい。
examples.romaji: Haha ga tsukuru ryōri no yō ni oishiku tsukuritai.
examples.tr: I want to cook as deliciously as the food my mother makes.

pitfalls: Put の between the noun and ような: 花のような, not 花ような.
Choose ような before a noun and ように before a verb or adjective.
